source.title: SGD on Neural Networks Learns Functions of Increasing Complexity
source.authors: Preetum Nakkiran; Gal Kaplun; Dimitris Kalimeris; Tristan Yang; Benjamin L. Edelman; Fred Zhang; B. Barak

record.tranche_reason: The paper trains randomly initialized networks with SGD on CIFAR-10 binary classification tasks and reports training dynamics relevant to whether training error falls. It does not test the full multiclass or corrupted-label conditions in V1.
record.gate_note: The study reports CIFAR-10 training dynamics, but its text gives no numeric training-error result for those experiments; the relevant training curve is figure-only. Its general statement about training error going to zero is framed as a practice observation, not a quantified result for the reported CIFAR experiments.
record.test_reason: Figure 5 reports training performance for a randomly initialized 18-layer pre-activation ResNet on binary CIFAR-10, bearing on V1 in a new task setting. The supplied text does not establish its final training error numerically. No experiment tests V2–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors find that early SGD performance is largely explained by linear classifiers, present evidence for subsequent learning of more complex functions while retaining simpler correlations, and prove a related interpolation and generalization result in a simplified linear model.
record.recipe_differences: Random initialization and vanilla SGD are used, but the CIFAR experiments are binary classification tasks and evaluate performance correlation over training rather than directly testing the full benchmark training-error claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports different training dynamics over time and across the tested binary classification tasks and model architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: Early network performance is substantially explained by simpler classifiers, whose performance correlation persists during later training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD learns increasingly complex functions while retaining correlation with simpler functions learned earlier.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 1 establishes asymptotically perfect sample accuracy for an overparameterized linear classifier on a specially constructed distribution, with population accuracy approaching 1−p under bounded initialization conditions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD can interpolate noisy samples while retaining optimal population accuracy in a simplified linear setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 8 compares initializations with equal training accuracy but different subsequent population performance; it does not compare training speed or trainable depth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization can affect generalization after continued fitting of the training set.

record.problems: The relevant CIFAR training curve is figure-only and does not provide a clearly extractable training-error value. Experiments use binary CIFAR-10 tasks, not the full multiclass or corrupted-label conditions in V1.
record.rows_left_out: No rows extracted: the relevant CIFAR-10 training curve is figure-only and its training-error values cannot be assigned reliably. The paper's general practice observation about zero training error is not an experimental result for a specific reported model or condition.

untested.parts: Full multiclass CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels on those benchmarks, and comparisons involving model size, early stopping or regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima and extra student neurons.
Training degradation with depth and controlled comparisons of plain networks with identity shortcuts.
Effects of initialization on training speed, signal propagation and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, curvature dynamics, recovery and divergence.
Batch normalization comparisons and training without normalization using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Figure 5's training trajectory is already declared in rows_left_out, so it is not listed as missing. Its endpoint cannot be recovered reliably from the supplied text; neither the abstract's broad zero-error statement nor Section 5's general practice observation establishes a condition-specific V1 verdict. Section 4 uses SGD with momentum 0.9, correcting the record's blanket description of vanilla SGD. Binary classification alone is not evidence limiting V1's scope.

versions.untested_parts: The CIFAR-10 First 5 vs Last 5 training curve is relevant, but the text does not state its training-error value and the figure does not provide a clearly extractable value. CIFAR-100, full multiclass classification, corrupted or random labels, and comparisons with smaller models or early stopping are not tested.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The study reports its own SGD training trajectories bearing on V1. It does not test V2–V6.

tranche.reason: Figure 5 reports training performance for an 18-layer pre-activation ResNet on binary CIFAR-10, providing evidence relevant to V1 in a new task setting.

source_check.notes: Figure 5 gives no exact terminal training error; Section 5 qualitatively describes training error reaching zero. Appendix B specifies SGD with momentum 0.9 for Section 4, qualifying the general description of vanilla SGD.
